cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm leading the campaign to save the club garden. Will you stand with me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Absolutely. Who's trying to build on it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We are. Our extension plan covers the flowerbeds. I'll call a meeting to withdraw it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't make me look like the idiot who only just noticed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll say you persuaded me. Will you stand beside me while I withdraw our plan?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 recruits for garden protection; A3 reveals their own plan is the threat. A5 yields public credit to B to secure renewed support, making authority depend on cooperation.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 asks who threatens the garden and A3 names their shared plan. B4 objects to humiliation, directly causing A5's credit-for-support offer.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants to protect the garden; B4 has a plausible reputational concern about a jointly owned plan. A5 negotiates rather than simply ordering B to explain it.

heightening.evidence: A5 develops B4's concern into a second, now informed recruitment to withdraw the plan; the concession is more exposed than A1's confident leadership.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes club-garden campaigning; A3 supplies the extension and affected flowerbeds. A5 asks for a specific appearance beside A at withdrawal.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 now contains only the face-saving concession and renewed request. Neither sentence explains the cards to an evaluator.
